m.d: A sweet is a piece of candy.
If something is sweet, it tastes like sugar or fruit.
m.e: This cake is very sweet. I think you put much sugar in it.

m.d: A sweet person or thing pleases or is nice.
m.e: Thank you! It's very sweet of you to give me this.

m.d: A swear word; an impolite or offensive word.
When you swear, you say a swear word.
When you swear, you make a promise or an oath.
A sweetheart is someone you love in a romantic way.
m.e: My sweetheart gave me a box of candy on Valentine's Day.

m.d: Sweetie is something you call someone who you love, especially someone you love romantically.
A sweetie is someone who is sweet; they are kind and affectionate.
Another word for candy.
A sword is a weapon made of metal which is long, thin and sharp, like a very long knife.
m.e: Before there were guns, people used to use swords to fight and kill each other.

m.d: A switch is what you use to turn lights or other machines and equipment on and off.
m.e: The light switch is on the wall behind the door.

m.d: A switch is a change from one thing to another.
m.e: It's often difficult for older people to make the switch to living alone.

m.d: A switch is a place on the track where trains can chose between two tracks.
If you switch something, you change it to something else.
m.e: He switched his book with mine.

m.d: If you switch a light or machine on, you change something so that it has power and can work.
m.e: She sat up in bed and switched on the light.

m.d: If you switch a light or machine off, you change something so that it doesn't have power and can't work.
m.e: I switched off the computer and went to bed.

m.d: A swim is when someone swims.
m.e: We all went for a swim in the lake.

m.d: If you swim, you move through the water using your arms and legs.
m.e: Let's go swimming at the beach.

m.d: A swing is a hanging seat found in a playground that children can sit on and swing on.
m.e: The child was swinging on the swing at the playground.

m.d: Swing is a style of dance.
Swing is the genre of dance linked to the style of dance.
If someone or something swings, they move forward and backward.
m.e: The plant swung in the breeze.

m.d: If someone swings, he dances.
If someone swings, they ride on a swingset.
Swimming is the act of propelling oneself through water using the limbs.
A salty water that is produced naturally by the body.
m.e: It is so hot that my whole body is covered with sweat!

m.d: A natural occurrence of the body to allow the body to cool by excreting salty water (see above).
m.e: You are sweating so much!

m.d: A swallow is a kind of small bird.
A swallow is the amount of food or liquid that goes down the throat at one time.
A swallow is the act of swallowing.
m.e: He took the aspirin with a single swallow of water.

m.d: If you swallow something you make it go through your mouth into your body (down your esophagus to your stomach). We swallow food and drinks.
m.e: Young children put small toys in their mouths and sometimes swallow them.

m.d: When something swells, it becomes larger, usually due to an increase in blood in an area of the body.
When you sweep the floor, you use the broom to clean it.
m.e: The road cleaner swept the roads clean.

m.d: A sweater is a warm piece of clothing people mostly wear during winter.
A swamp is an area where most of the land is underwater. Land in a swamp is not usually more than a meter (or a few feet) under water.
m.e: We were wading through the swamp.

m.d: If something is swamped it is being covered of filled with water.
m.e: The deck of our boat was swamped by the storm.

m.d: If something is swamped is has gotten more of something than it can work with.
m.e: Our office was swamped with phone calls.

m.d: Switzerland is a country in central Europe.
A Swiss is a person or thing that comes from Switzerland.
Something or someone that is Swiss comes from Switzerland.
m.e: The Swiss currency is the Swiss franc.

m.d: Swedish is the language of Sweden and Åland.
Something or someone that is Swedish comes from Sweden.
m.e: The Swedish currency is the Krona.

m.d: A swan is a waterbird with a long neck. They are usually white, but in Australia they are black.
m.e: The swan used its long neck to find food on the bottom of the lake

m.d: Sweden is a country in the north of Europe.
A swine is a technical or archaic word for a pig, for example the term swine flu is still used today.
A swine is a derogatory word for a man regarded as mean or contemptible.
A swap is an exchange.
m.e: I think that our swap was a bad idea.

m.d: If you swap one thing for another, you give one thing to somebody and they give you the other thing.
m.e: I like your pencil and you like my pen. Let's swap, shall we?

m.d: If a person is sweaty, they are covered in sweat.
If something is swift, it is fast.
m.e: A swift hit on the head should keep him unconscious for an hour.

m.d: If you sway, you move slowly from side to side.
The sweetness of a food, plant, chemical, etc. is how sweet it is.
Your sweetness is how kind you are.
A swimmer is someone who swims or has the ability to swim.
m.e: Michael Phelps is a professional swimmer.

m.d: A swarm is a group of many insects, especially flying insects like bees, wasps or flies.
m.e: He walked on a wasp nest and was attacked by the swarm.

m.d: Less commonly, a swarm can also be a group of fish or birds.
m.e: When attacked, sardinas group into compact swarms to protect themselves.

m.d: A crowd of people or animals moving in a chaotic way.
To move as a swarm.
m.e: I felt disgusted when I saw all these flies swarming on this dead body.

m.d: When there are to many insects in a place.
m.e: Fire ants swarm in the Southern United States since man accidentally brought some with him by ship.

m.d: To fill a place as a swarm.
m.e: Ants are swarming the kitchen since we let food accessible.

m.d: A swipe is a quick grab, bat, or other motion with the hand or paw.
A swipe is a strong blow given with a sweeping motion.
If you swipe, you grab or bat something quickly.
If you swipe something, you hit it with a strong blow in a sweeping motion.
If you swipe a card, you scan or register it by sliding it through a reader.
If you do something swiftly, you do it quickly or at a high speed.
A swimsuit is a piece of clothing that fits close to your body that you wear when you swim.
m.e: Put on your swimsuit and let's go for a swim.

m.d: If a bird swoops, it flies or glides downwards suddenly.
If you are swamped, you are very busy.
m.e: I'd love to meet you for lunch, but I'm way too swamped.

m.d: A sweatshirt is a loose shirt that is usually made of cotton. It is worn when exercising or as a casual apparel.
A swede is a yellow root vegetable, like a turnip.
m.e: He really enjoyed a dinner of fish with boiled swedes and peas.

m.d: A Swede is a person from Sweden.
m.e: Alfred Nobel is a famous Swede, who gave the money for the Nobel Prizes.

m.d: A person's swagger is their confidence and pride.
If a person swaggers, they behave in a confident and arrogant way.
A swindler is a person who tricks or cheats other people for their money.
A swindle is the deception of money-related items.
If you swindle someone out of money, you trick them into giving you the money.
A swirl is something that is moving in a twisting or spiraling pattern.
If something is swirling, it is move in a twisting or spiraling pattern.
If you sweeten something, you make it sweeter.
m.e: They offer me hot milk sweetened with sugar.

m.d: If you sweeten a deal or an offer, you make it better for the other person.
m.e: I might agree to that if you sweetened the deal.
